import json

def time_to_minutes(t):

def main():
    # Input variables (constraints)
    start_location = "Russian Hill"
    start_time_str = "9:00"

    people = [
        {"name": "Mark", "location": "Marina District", "start": "18:45", "end": "21:00", "min_minutes": 90},
        {"name": "Karen", "location": "Financial District", "start": "9:30", "end": "12:45", "min_minutes": 90},
        {"name": "Barbara", "location": "Alamo Square", "start": "10:00", "end": "19:30", "min_minutes": 90},

        {"name": "Andrew", "location": "Nob Hill", "start": "11:45", "end": "16:45", "min_minutes": 105},
    ]

    # Preprocess times
    for p in people:
        p["start_min"] = time_to_minutes(p["start"])
        p["end_min"] = time_to_minutes(p["end"])

    # Build travel times
    travel = build_travel()

    # Map locations to ensure presence in travel matrix
    locations = set(travel.keys())
    for p in people:
        locations.add(p["location"])
    locations.add(start_location)

    # Person indices and lookup
    name_to_idx = {p["name"]: i for i, p in enumerate(people)}

    # Sort people by window end to guide search (heuristic)
    order = sorted(range(len(people)), key=lambda i: people[i]["end_min"])

    # DFS search with backtracking to maximize meetings
    from functools import lru_cache

    START_TIME = time_to_minutes(start_time_str)

    # Build a list of candidates per state dynamically; we use caching for states
    @lru_cache(maxsize=None)
    def search(current_loc, current_time, met_mask):
        best_count = 0
        best_end_time = current_time
        best_itinerary = []

        # Generate feasible next meetings
        candidates = []
        for i in order:
            if (met_mask >> i) & 1:
                continue
            person = people[i]
            # Travel time
            if current_loc not in travel or person["location"] not in travel[current_loc]:
                continue
            t_arrive = current_time + travel[current_loc][person["location"]]
            t_start = max(t_arrive, person["start_min"])
            t_end = t_start + person["min_minutes"]
            if t_end <= person["end_min"]:
                candidates.append((t_start, t_end, i, person["location"]))

        # Order candidates by earliest feasible start then end to reduce branching
        candidates.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1]))

        # Simple optimistic bound: remaining people count cannot exceed len(remaining)
        remaining_possible = len([i for i in range(len(people)) if not ((met_mask >> i) & 1)])
        # If even taking all remaining we cannot beat best found in this call, we'll still explore because best_count here is only local.

        for t_start, t_end, i, loc in candidates:
            person = people[i]
            new_mask = met_mask | (1 << i)
            sub_count, sub_end, sub_it = search(loc, t_end, new_mask)
            total_count = 1 + sub_count
            total_end = sub_end if sub_it else t_end  # if no further meetings, end at this meeting end
            total_it = [{"action": "meet", "location": person["location"], "person": person["name"],
                         "start_time": minutes_to_time(t_start), "end_time": minutes_to_time(t_end)}] + sub_it
            if (total_count > best_count) or (total_count == best_count and total_end < best_end_time):
                best_count = total_count
                best_end_time = total_end
                best_itinerary = total_it

            # Prune if we already met all people
            if best_count == len(people) - bin(met_mask).count("1"):
                break

        return best_count, best_end_time, best_itinerary

    best_count, best_end, best_it = search(start_location, START_TIME, 0)

    # Build output JSON
    result = {
        "itinerary": best_it
    }
    print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False))
